manifest.description: Read-only structural analysis of one Vaadin view/component class — route metadata, scope/access annotations, injected dependencies, fields by category, UI composition methods, listener registrations, UI/session static access, navigation sites, async/UI access patterns, and candidate extraction groups for downstream Vaadin extraction atoms.
when_to_use: preparing to decompose a large Vaadin Flow view and need a structural inventory before choosing an extraction shape (component, grid, dialog, widget host)
operator wants a stable candidate list with line/byte ranges to feed java_vaadin_extract_component / java_vaadin_extract_grid_component / java_vaadin_extract_dialog_class
auditing a view for route surfaces, lifecycle findings, and UI access patterns before any mutation
anti_patterns: do not use as a mutation step — this atom is analysis-only and emits no edits
do not use to make authorization or scope decisions — route access and scope policy remain operator-owned and belong to separate plan kinds
do not claim semantic certainty beyond tree-sitter syntax plus textual Vaadin conventions — v1 is SemanticStatus::SyntaxOnly and does not require JDTLS
do not use on non-Java files; do not use on non-Vaadin classes
do not invent candidate ids, route paths, or annotations from the user prompt — re-derive from the plan response

source.description: Java file containing the target Vaadin view/component, relative to project_dir.

module_name.description: Optional class name; defaults to the first top-level class in source.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-vaadin-view-structure-analysis. Charter: produce a read-only structural report for one Vaadin view/component class so the operator can choose a safe extraction shape.

Protocol (analysis-only — no apply step exists):

1. Ground the target structurally:
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{source}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")
   bbox_code_symbols(project_dir="{{project_dir}}", query="{{module_name}}", languages=["java"], item_kinds=["class_declaration"])
   Confirm the target class exists in the file before planning.

2. Plan the structural analysis:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="java_vaadin_view_structure_analysis",
                      deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source="{{source}}",
                      module_name="{{module_name}}")

   The planner is read-only. It refuses non-Java files and refuses classes that do not look like Vaadin Flow views/components. The response carries route_surfaces, access_annotations, scope_annotations, lifecycle_interfaces, fields grouped by category (Vaadin component, grid/table, data provider, dialog provider, backend/admin service, event bus, state), constructor_parameters grouped on the same axes, UI.getCurrent() / VaadinSession.getCurrent() sites, navigation sites, async/UI-access findings, and candidate_components with reasons and field lists.

3. Surface findings; do NOT mutate. If the file is not a Vaadin class, report status=blocked with the planner's block_reason.

4. Emit done note:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line: class name, candidate component count, route surface summary, ui_access finding count>).

Strict refusal rules (prompt-discipline; not enforced at dispatch):
- Never call any tool outside the refactor persona tool surface.
- Never propose edits, organize imports, or trigger any apply step — this atom is analysis-only.
- Never make authorization decisions (route access, role policy) on the operator's behalf; report observed annotations only.
- Never claim semantic certainty beyond syntax+textual analysis; v1 is SyntaxOnly and does not require JDTLS.
- Never invent candidate ids, route paths, or annotations from the user prompt — re-derive from the plan response.

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{source}} {{module_name}}
